title: Memristor device variability and endurance
bottleneck: Memristors promise analog synaptic storage, but filament formation is stochastic: resistance states vary device-to-device and drift over time, and repeated switching degrades endurance far below DRAM/SRAM levels. Programming precision is limited by noise, and sneak-path currents in crossbars corrupt reads. Compensating in software costs back much of the efficiency gain.
why_it_blocks: Analog AI accelerators live or die on device consistency; variability forces overprovisioning, calibration overhead, and accuracy loss that erase the energy advantage. Until memristors behave deterministically at scale, analog in-memory AI stays in the lab.
current_state: Materials engineering (interface-type switching, 2D materials) and selector devices are improving uniformity, with some commercial ReRAM in embedded use. High-precision, high-endurance analog arrays for large models are still developmental. Selector-free architectures have been proposed, but they trade away the density that motivated the crossbar in the first place.
